subject: Mutual Action Plan + Marketplace private-offer path for FinTechCo evaluation
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Scott <amelia@fintechco.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual Action Plan proposal & private-offer route for evaluation

Hi Amelia,

Great talking earlier — appreciate the clear priorities on latency and data isolation for your payments ML workloads. As discussed, I sketched a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that ties evaluation milestones to concrete commercial steps and a marketplace private-offer flow so procurement can track discounts against commitments. I attached a lightweight MAP template you can share with internal stakeholders.

High-level MAP (proposal):
- Week 0–2: Sandbox evaluation (no committed spend) — Redwood provides 30 days of trial credits + dedicated support.
- Week 2–6: POC (customer test suite) — goal: sign-off on quality bar + latency SLO. Trigger: POC sign-off doc.
- Week 6–8: Procurement window — we issue AWS private offer and DocuSign term-sheet mapped to MAP milestones.
- Month 1–3 post-PO: On-ramp: $50k mo (tier 1) -> Month 4+ ramp to $150k mo (tier 2). Discount schedule below.

Pricing / discount suggestion (MAP-linked):
- No commit (trial): no discount, usage billing via hosted API.
- Commit Tier 1 (>= $50k/month): 12% discount off list private-offer price.
- Commit Tier 2 (>= $150k/month): 22% discount + 90-day price lock.
- Accelerators: 10% one-time onboarding credit for early signing within MAP window.

Why marketplace private-offer? Procurement prefers a PO-backed private-offer in AWS Marketplace (or GCP equivalent) for single-invoice flow and faster approvals. We can mirror the private-offer terms across both AWS and GCP if you want multi-cloud protection.

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_template.xlsx (live MAP), rwd_quote_aws_private_offer.pdf (draft pricing).

Next steps I suggest:
1) Review MAP template with your procurement & security by Friday 7/3.
2) We’ll update private-offer term sheet and provision an AWS private-offer draft for your procurement to review by 7/6.
3) Target DocuSign for signature by 7/10 to enable on-ramp mid-July.

If you want, I can loop Karthik (pricing) into procurement threads; he can lock final tiering and PS credits.

Thanks — talk soon,

Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Amelia Scott <amelia@fintechco.com>

Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 09:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan proposal & private-offer route for evaluation

Thanks, Sergio — this is helpful and the MAP format looks good for our stakeholders. A few items from our side:

- Security: our security team will need a SOC2 report + evidence of KV cache isolation for tenant-separated inference. Can Laura help route those artifacts?
- Procurement: we prefer the AWS private-offer path (single vendor PO). Please ensure the private-offer includes an explicit PO line for committed monthly spend and the discount table mapped to the MAP milestones.
- Timeline: the business wants POC sign-off in early July; procurement can only review private-offers the week of 7/6. Is that alignment workable?

Also adding Jordan Patel (Procurement) on copy — Jordan, are there any non-standard contract items we should flag now (e.g., data residency or additional indemnities)?

Best,
Amelia
Head of Product, FinTechCo
amelia@fintechco.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Scott <amelia@fintechco.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Security Team <security@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan proposal & private-offer route for evaluation

Amelia — happy to coordinate. Quick answers and an operational proposal from the CS side: 

- Security artifacts: I’ve attached the SOC2 cover note and will drop a link to our compliance pack in the shared Drive folder. Security can provide an architecture note on KV cache segregation for your infra team.
- MAP operationalization: To keep procurement happy, we will publish a private-offer term sheet that maps each MAP milestone to a deliverable (e.g., POC sign-off -> private-offer activation; DocuSign signature -> billing start date). See attached private_offer_term_sheet.pdf.
- Proposed on-ramp schedule:
   * POC sign-off -> Issue AWS private-offer draft (procurement review window 7/6–7/10)
   * If PO returned within 7 business days -> onboarding window starts and we apply onboarding credit.

Note on pricing mechanics: AWS private-offer will reference an annualized spend commitment with monthly invoicing per your PO. For elasticity, we can include a clause allowing bursts above committed baseline billed at list price unless you upgrade tiers.

I’ll queue Security to send the SOC2 and architecture note by EOD 7/3. Sergio — I suggest you loop Karthik in for final quote approval before we send the private-offer to Jordan.

Laura Bennett
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0333

Sergio / Laura — Jordan from Procurement here. A few procurement/legal clarifications so we can route the AWS private-offer quickly: 

1) PO visibility: We need the private-offer to list the exact monthly committed minimum and the discount tiers with start/end dates.
2) Term and termination: We generally run 12-month terms for marketplace private-offers; need cancellation terms and early-termination fees spelled out.
3) Data residency / audit: Please confirm whether logs (audit + request traces) can be exported to our S3 bucket and what retention options exist.

Action items for Redwood: please send a private-offer draft PDF and a one-page summary that procurement can push through our internal marketplace approval flow. Also send a DocuSign-ready term-sheet that procurement can sign against a PO.

Jordan Patel
Senior Procurement Manager, FinTechCo
jordan.patel@fintechco.com

Jordan / Amelia — thanks for the clear asks. We updated materials and are ready to move: 

What we delivered today (links/attachments):
- AWS private-offer draft (rwd_quote_aws_private_offer.pdf) — includes committed monthly baseline, discount tiers, 12-month term, and early-termination clause (90 days notice + prorated refund rules).
- Private-offer term-sheet (private_offer_term_sheet.pdf) — DocuSign-ready, maps MAP milestones to billing triggers. DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/finish/2a3b4c5d
- MAP checklist (Redwood_MAP_template.xlsx) in shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bMAP-FinTechCo

Key commercial mapping (finalized):
- MAP milestone: POC sign-off -> private-offer activation (no billing until DocuSign + PO received).
- MAP milestone: Signed PO (first month commit $50k) -> apply Tier 1 discount (12%) and onboarding credit of 10% against month 1 invoice.
- MAP milestone: Ramp to >= $150k/month sustained for 2 consecutive months -> automatic upgrade to Tier 2 pricing (22% discount) and 90-day price lock.

Security & audit: Laura confirmed SOC2 + audit-readiness artifacts uploaded to the Drive folder; logs can be exported to a customer-controlled S3 bucket (retention configurable, default 90 days).

Next steps / ask list:
1) Jordan: can you confirm procurement will accept the private-offer draft format? If yes, we’ll send DocuSign for signature and provision the AWS private-offer record.
2) Amelia: confirm POC sign-off criteria (I’ve put a short checklist in the Drive MAP).
3) Karthik: please confirm final pricing numbers (I’ve CCed you to approve the quote).

If procurement can sign by 7/10 we can target a 7/15 onboarding start date. 

Thanks — Sergio
